messages.content: I've changed my mind, can I get a greens instead of what I previously ordered?

function.name: ChaFod
function.description: Changes the selection of food based on the customer's request, ensuring the food name provided is in uppercase as per the requirement. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

TheFod.description: The name of the food to be changed, provided in uppercase letters only (e.g., 'PIZZA', 'BURGER').

message.reasoning: User wants to change order to greens. We have function ChaFod that changes selection of food based on customer's request. It expects TheFod: "PIZZA" | "BURGER" | "SALAD" | "SOUP" | "STEAK". Greens is not in list. But maybe we can interpret "greens" as "SALAD"? The user says "greens" instead of what they previously ordered. We need to respond with a function call. But the function only accepts those options. We could choose SALAD. But we need to ensure uppercase. So we call ChaFod with TheFod: "SALAD". That will change selection to salad. That might satisfy. But we should also mention that we changed to salad. But we can't output text besides function call. According to instruction: "When you do want to call a function, you must do so in the form of a function call. Do not provide any additional text or explanation." So we must only output function call. So we call ChaFod with TheFod: "SALAD".
